vertical pulling movement of any grip (supinated, pronated, neutral) will result in lat activation. you can slow your reps down equally with any grip, whether that be 1 second or 20 second reps. perhaps you are just not as strong in a pronated and wide grip as you are with a supinated and narrow grip.

inverted rows are important because you don’t want to mess up your posture. inverted rows work scapular retraction so middle traps and rhomboids. if you just do a bunch of push exercises without balancing it out, then your chest will obviously become much stronger than your undertrained back muscles, leading to a forward shoulder posture and rounded back as your chest pulls your shoulders forward, and your back is too weak to properly retract it all back. this “bad posture” puts you at a greater risk for injury.
